thesisQuality.note: About 230M lb uranium commitments and 83M kgU UF6 contracted across global utility customers demonstrate durable demand and value capture; tier-one assets and fuel services add differentiation.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: First-half 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $899M with $1.1B cash, $1.0B debt and an undrawn $1.0B revolver, but quarter-level production/logistics and Westinghouse variability temper the band.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: At Sep. 18 the market cap was about US$39.8B with trailing P/E about 159x, P/S about 16.3x and P/FCF about 100x, a demanding valuation relative to current earnings/cash flow despite structural growth.

catalystScore.note: Long-term uranium contracting, improving pricing, maintained 2026 production guidance and increased Cigar Lake ownership are material identifiable catalysts, though timing remains variable.

governancePower.note: 2026 proxy documents established board governance, shareholder voting and compensation disclosure; balance-sheet discipline and selective market-related contracting support stewardship, without evidence sufficient for an exceptional band.

alignment2036.note: Uranium, conversion/fuel services and Westinghouse reactor technology directly serve durable nuclear electricity, life-extension and energy-security needs across multiple regions.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: Uranium, fuel services and Westinghouse provide distinct demand engines; uranium contracts span 39 customers and fuel services 33 customers in 16 countries, though customer concentration remains meaningful.

bottleneckControl.note: Tier-one uranium assets, record conversion production and contracted fuel-service volumes place Cameco across scarce nuclear fuel-cycle nodes; increased Cigar Lake ownership deepens control.

scenarioRobustness.note: Geographic customer diversity, uranium/fuel-services/Westinghouse exposure and flexible contract structures provide several paths to value, offset by nuclear-cycle and site-specific concentration.

substitutionResilience.note: Long-lived utility contracts, specialized fuel-cycle facilities and reactor-service capabilities create qualification and replacement friction, but enrichment/conversion alternatives and competing uranium supply remain substitutes.

supplyChainResilience.note: Inventory, purchases, contract/logistics management and multiple business segments provide buffers, while remote mine exposure and concentrated high-quality assets leave meaningful dependencies.

pricingPower.note: Fuel-services realized pricing improved under contracts signed in a better price environment; uranium contracting deliberately preserves market-related upside and downside protection, supporting pricing power short of exceptional certainty.

risk.note: Remote-mine disruptions, delivery timing, Westinghouse project variability, five-largest-customer concentration at 56% of uranium commitments, and demanding valuation create material but not thesis-breaking risk.

confidence.note: Core operating, contracting, liquidity and governance claims are primary-source addressed and current valuation is independently dated; future contract mix and Westinghouse IPO economics remain unknown and reduce confidence.

thesis: Cameco is a diversified nuclear fuel-cycle and reactor-technology exposure with contracted demand and scarce assets positioned for long-duration nuclear growth, offset by operational concentration and a demanding valuation.
keyRisk: High valuation and site/project execution variability can compress per-share returns even if nuclear demand remains structurally favorable.
nextCatalyst: Next scheduled earnings and operating update, expected October 30, 2026, plus continued uranium contracting and pricing disclosures.
